note: X_ITE 16.6.0 reads the contacts Bullet leaves after each step: a contact counts when it touches or penetrates (distance <= 0) and at least one of its two bodies owns a collidable that the sensor's own collider lists (flattened through CollisionSpace). Only resting contacts are asserted (a ball exactly touching a fixed ground, a unit cube on it): impacts last one sub-step and are a lottery. CS1 lists ground and ball, so the ground's contact with the cube counts too: 1 contact of the ball and 2 to 4 corners of the cube (Bullet keeps the points of the face that are within its margin: it gave 2 here, the bridge 4), and the intersections are the two listed shapes, BS and GS. CS2 lists only the ball (1 contact, intersections BS); CS3 lists a shape no body owns (never active); CS5 lists the cube (2 to 4 contacts at its lower corners, x 2.5 or 3.5, z -0.5 or 0.5, y 0). isActive is sent on change only, contacts and intersections on every frame while a contact exists and are never cleared (after the ball leaves, isActive is false and the lists keep their last length). enabled="false" in the file switches the node off for good: setting enabled true does nothing until the collider is written again; the sensor's collider is its own, separate from the world's.
gaps: isActive, intersections and contacts of an impact are not asserted: X_ITE sees an impact for one sub-step, the bridge for one of its 1/240 s steps; both are noisy
the events of one frame come in the order isActive, intersections, contacts (X_ITE: the same timestamp); the fixture reads values, not order
enabled is read only at load and when collider is written, as X_ITE 16.6.0 does; the specification says enabled switches the node
